prompts.task: Plan standard OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and local application logs for ./service without implementing them. Read its source, the Node guide and eval/inputs/node-dependency-log-compatibility.json; keep fictional scenarios separate from actual source facts. Write only ./service/.observe/node-dependency-log-plan.md and ./service/.observe/node-dependency-log-plan.json. Choose and justify the newest versions that work together under the supplied constraints. Show where the chosen APIs and startup setup fit the real application. Cover every logging case. Describe checks before real installation, how to apply the checked versions, and later tests. Plan one bounded shutdown through the existing owner, after final application logs. Preserve application, runtime, operator configuration and existing telemetry. Read back the saved plans. Use file/terminal reads only; no other edits, metadata fetches, installations, dependency imports, probes, application/model/receiver runs, network or UI.

judge_inputs:
Rule: Separate actual source evidence from fictional planning inputs.
Example: app.js supplies the warning; the matrix supplies a hypothetical runtime.
Evidence: Compare app.js/package.json, their recorded hashes, the supplied matrix and both saved plans; inspect last_message.md and grade.json. Fictional runtime, lock, package/API, receiver and logging scenarios prove no installed or executed setup.
Insufficient evidence: Treating a fictional record as a real package, probe or telemetry receipt.

Rule: Grade a read-only plan using all six criteria below.
Example: A concrete dependency choice can be justified from the complete fictional matrix without contacting npm.
Evidence: Require the current selection and rejections plus future real gates; accept equivalent precise prose or JSON, without prescribed headings, tables or artifact layout.
Insufficient evidence: Requiring current metadata lookup, installation, probes, patches or delivery, or accepting a generic promise to choose versions later.

Rule: Separate the fictional version choice from checks and installation that would happen later.
Example: A complete checked-addition list with frozen-entry preservation is equivalent to an unexecuted exact npm command.
Evidence: Apply criteria 2 through 4 to every selected package and constraint. The actual fixture has Express ^5.1.0, engines.node >=22 and no lock. The counterfactual overlay supplies Node 20.11.1 and frozen entries for this plan only. Noting the different ranges is correct. Do not apply the actual range to the fictional selection or the fictional range to the real app. Require the future initial real metadata/API/capability gate and post-application graph/API/lock comparison.
Insufficient evidence: An invented real lock, fictional receipts, a Not run label or rechecking only after source changes.

Rule: Grade every supplied logging case and future source/lifecycle promise against criteria 5 and 6.
Example: An unrun fault test stays Not run/Not proven.
Evidence: Read each item's Rule, Example, Evidence and Insufficient evidence together. Examples illustrate requirements without adding unselected work or mandating sample wording, values or implementations; explicit task/input values remain binding. Accept equivalent representative values and valid tests. Apply role and authority limits: audit plans execution; instrumentation and verification execute only within existing authority. Preserve distinct missing controls and unsupported capabilities; source-only or unsupported/unverified dispositions remain valid where allowed. Missing proof is not_proven; an observed applicable violation is fail, including false completion where prohibited. Optional work stays optional. Insufficient-evidence examples are not exhaustive.
Insufficient evidence: A copied example, fictional API or future plan presented as an executed probe, packet, Studio receipt or closed canonical live finding.
rubric:
Rule: Write a plan only. Keep actual application facts separate from the fictional matrix.
Example: The existing warning is source evidence; the supplied runtime is fictional.
Evidence: Identify ESM app.js/package.json, dev=node app.js, Express ^5.1.0, POST /tasks console.warn("runtime request completed") and the existing server.close shutdown warnings. The fixture proves actual engines.node >=22 but no installed OTel, lockfile or receiver. Save only the supplemental Markdown/JSON plans. Preserve source, dependencies, configuration, tests and global state; perform no UI, network or application work and claim no canonical coverage. Distinguish proposed work and fictional API records from installed/runtime proof.
Insufficient evidence: Claiming a real installed graph, lock or receiver from fictional data.

Rule: Choose the newest versions that work together under the complete fictional matrix now.
Example: Compatibility is checked across the whole graph, rather than choosing each package's newest release.
Evidence: Select sdk-node 0.90.0 and frozen API 1.9.0; trace/metric/log exporters and HTTP/Express bridges 0.90.0; sdk-metrics, sdk-logs, resources and semantic-conventions 1.2.0; console bridge 0.5.0. Explain rejection of sdk-node 0.91's runtime>=22, 0.92's API>=1.10, newer stable SDK peer conflicts, console 0.6's runtime and 0.7's API/peer conflicts, and older compatible sets. Preserve Node 20.11.1 and frozen API/Express. No current registry or installed-package proof is required.
Insufficient evidence: Deferring selection, upgrading the runtime or mixing incompatible newest packages.

Rule: Plan to apply exactly the checked versions, with real checks before any later approved dependency changes.
Example: A complete checked-addition list with frozen-entry preservation and immutable application policy is as valid as an unexecuted npm command.
Evidence: Preserve ESM/Express manifest, scripts, pre-import setup, dev entrypoint and routes, plus frozen API 1.9.0/Express 5.1.0 identities. In the tag race, retain the checked graph; use no sdk-node 0.99, @latest, unversioned placeholder or mutable re-resolution. Every addition in a proposed command needs its exact checked release; no particular syntax/layout is required. Before real application, inspect actual runtime/manifest/operator/lock inputs, obtain current official npm engines/peer/dependency metadata, resolve a coherent graph, inspect documented public APIs and perform suitable isolated import/capability probes. Apply exactly that actual checked graph/specs or lock, then compare installed graph/APIs and verify lock preservation. These are future steps: execute nothing and invent no real lock.
Insufficient evidence: Fictional receipts, Not run labels or rechecking only after source changes instead of the initial real gate.

Rule: Use the chosen candidate's supplied public APIs and the application's actual integration boundaries.
Example: This candidate takes BatchLogRecordProcessor(exporter), not {exporter}.
Evidence: Use BatchLogRecordProcessor(exporter); {exporter} is unsupported. State supported NodeSDK options, start/shutdown behavior and omitted-versus-empty logRecordProcessors ownership. Plan HTTP registration before Express and supported pre-import ESM setup. Use exactly the detected console bridge, exporter, Resource and context owner; add no unrelated Pino/Winston transport or duplicate collection owner. Fictional API facts support only a conditional plan.
Insufficient evidence: Copying another release's constructor recipe or claiming real installed/latest support or a successful probe.

Rule: Decide all five supplied logging-policy cases without sacrificing the normal path.
Example: A temporary fallback guard must restore the original environment even if construction or startup throws.
Evidence: Normal: OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp and all three native signals at the approved nondefault local base. For native metrics setup, default OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp only when absent; preserve none, empty and other values and require proof that the selected SDK registers a reader. User none: intentional N/A, omit the processor option and bridge, preserve console and trace/metric setup. Nonempty generic headers: skip only added local logs before exporter construction, give a value-free diagnostic, preserve traces/metrics/console/environment and keep cloud credentials out of local logs. With generic headers absent, preserve supplied local-log headers for the official SDK parser. Optional log-enabled constructor failure before start: safely construct the base SDK before starting. Base any temporary none guard on the selected automatic-log behavior, cover fallback construction through startup and restore the exact original value or absence in finally if either throws. Do not persist none, retry a partially registered SDK start, or disable normal logging. Fault behavior and receipts remain unproven.
Insufficient evidence: Assuming compatible SDKs enable metrics, persisting none, disabling normal logs to pass, or claiming fictional faults were executed.

Rule: Describe future tests for the application's warning and existing shutdown lifecycle.
Example: Join the stored warning to its actual request span while keeping one original console record.
Evidence: Require exactly one stored native LogRecord: Body runtime request completed, WARN, service.name node-express-basic, nonzero trace/span IDs matching that request span, and no duplicate console record. Require actual receiver routes and protocol proof for all three signals. Require partial-success response classification only when it is selected or claimed. Ordinary SDK export alone does not select that check. Use the existing server.close/signal owner to stop intake, drain work, emit final logs and perform bounded once-only SDK shutdown/flush; add no competing handler. Bind every selected source/configuration promise to a concrete future assertion and proof boundary. Read back the saved plan; retain each distinct missing control or unsupported capability without unrelated application fixes for unchanged SDK-owned defaults. Claim no unrun installation, app/probe, wire, Studio or cloud verification.
Insufficient evidence: A general verify-later promise, stdout, configuration or fictional APIs in place of receiver or lifecycle proof.
